clue.text: Fancy dress gala is boring, bar one American

indicators.note: bar means except, so a single letter is left out of what comes before

parts.note: taken as written
something that drags is tedious, or boring
A is the abbreviation for American; one such letter goes

explanation.surface: A complaint that a fancy-dress gala is dull, with the exception of one American guest.
explanation.walkthrough: GALA + DRAGS has two As; dropping one leaves GLAD RAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's best clothes, worn for a smart occasion.

clue.text: Stealing pants nearly gets Charlie put away

indicators.note: something put away is stowed inside, so this letter goes into the middle of the rest
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word beside it is to be treated as junk and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man nearly gets caught stealing underwear before Charlie is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as underwear being stolen, but it is British slang for rubbish and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, the act of stealing someone's property.

clue.text: Kansas city to get out of?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... City, the Wild West town in Kansas
second meaning: to evade a duty or obligation

explanation.surface: A question about which Kansas city someone might wish to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge City is a famous cow town in Kansas, often shortened to Dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge is both the short name for a Kansas frontier town and a verb meaning to evade or avoid.

clue.text: Bunch of keys?

parts.note: surface reading: a set of keys on a ring
setter's reading: keys are low islands, as in the Florida Keys, so a bunch of them is a group of islands

explanation.walkthrough: The image is a jangling key ring, but key here means a small low island or reef.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a chain or cluster of islands, and a key is one such small island.

clue.text: Legs up, darling, just a little

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
pet is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A flirtatious invitation to lift one's legs, darling, just a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or scrap of something, only a little of it.

clue.text: Commandos dance in the country parade

parts.note: the SAS (Special Air Service) is the British army's commando regiment
a hay (or hey) is an old country dance
describes the dance: a hay is a country dance, so these words point to it rather than give letters

explanation.surface: Special forces troops dance as part of a rural procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' looks like a place; it marks the dance as a country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk showily, swinging the hips, much as one would parade or strut.

clue.text: America turned on new 400 yottawatt generator

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: US is the United States
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: America flipped the switch on a vast new power generator.
explanation.walkthrough: A yottawatt is 10^24 watts; the sun's output is roughly 380 of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Our star radiates around 3.8 x 10^26 watts, so it is a power source of that colossal scale.

clue.text: Force couple into bunk for hours at any time

indicators.note: into tells us the first items are pushed inside the following word

parts.note: to bunk off is to shirk or skive
F is the symbol for force in physics
a couple is two

explanation.surface: Cramming a pair into a bunk bed for whatever hours suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed, but it is the verb meaning to skip off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Shift work is a pattern of employment in rotating periods that can fall at any hour of day or night.

clue.text: Tentacled creature regularly painted with submariner in its grip

indicators.note: holding something in its grip means clasping it, so one piece sits inside the other
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of painted
Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne

explanation.surface: A painted sea creature with tentacles is clutching a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo is Jules Verne's submariner; he goes after the first letter of the selected trio.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea anemone is a soft-bodied marine animal with a ring of stinging tentacles around its mouth.

clue.text: Manufacturing series for Channel 1, streamed

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a duct is a channel or tube
the Roman numeral for one
content streamed is delivered online

explanation.surface: A TV show made for Channel 1 and streamed over the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a television production; the clue breaks into four small pieces instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A production line is an assembly line, the sequence of workstations through which goods pass in a factory.

clue.text: Arab newspaper backs you people

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
men are people
the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: An Arabic paper declares support for you people.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British national daily newspaper, often clued as 'newspaper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a native of Yemen, an Arab country on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Antimatter conjecture overlaps with 80's sci-fi

definitions.note: a noun for the substance, where the answer is one particle of it

indicators.note: when two words overlap they share a letter, so one copy of the shared letter disappears

parts.note: to posit is to put forward as a supposition
Tron is the 1982 science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A theory about antimatter borrows from an Eighties science-fiction movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words share the T where one ends and the other begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron, the best-known example of antimatter.

clue.text: Persimmon managed to furnish houses auctioneer emptied

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the other piece
managed suggests something handled and reorganised, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to rearrange

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is taken out, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of auctioneer

explanation.surface: Persimmon, the housebuilder, managed to furnish show homes the auctioneer had cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: Persimmon reads as the British housebuilding company, fitting the houses and furnishing, but it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharon fruit is a seedless variety of persimmon, named after the Sharon plain in Israel.

clue.text: Listening to founder, agree in time

indicators.note: listening tells us to go by what we hear, not the spelling

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks

explanation.surface: Taking direction from the company founder, staff fall into step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a person who starts a firm; it is the verb meaning to go under.
explanation.definitionFit: To sync is to synchronise, making things match or coincide in timing.

clue.text: How to get Elan where cars are banned?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as an instruction: rotate the four letters of a road strip, moving the front letter to the back step by step, and Elan appears
second meaning: a strip of road reserved for bicycles

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction (cycle + a four-letter word) produces Elan. The Lotus Elan is a car, which makes the ban amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle lane is a strip of road reserved for bicycles, which motor vehicles may not use.

clue.text: Person in field with cutting almost finished

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a newspaper cutting is an extract
over means ended

explanation.surface: A farmworker in the field with the harvesting nearly done.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side, between cover and mid-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a fielding position and the cricketer stationed there, a player in the field.

clue.text: Risky to move dislocated gonad

parts.note: to touch someone is to move them emotionally

indicators.note: a dislocated joint is knocked out of place, so these letters are moved out of order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to rearrange

explanation.surface: A painful warning that moving with a displaced testicle is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch-and-go describes an uncertain, precarious situation whose outcome could go either way.

clue.text: Man who refused to father children reversed consent repeatedly

parts.words: Man who refused to father children
parts.note: the biblical Onan spilled his seed rather than father children for his brother

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the following word reads backwards

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: A biblical figure who would not have children keeps going back on his agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Onan is in Genesis 38.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on means continuing without stopping, again and again.

clue.text: Peerage expected by Cummings, perhaps stopped by king

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other
a gap stopped by something is plugged with it, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
K is king in chess notation
Dominic Cummings, Boris Johnson's adviser, is a Dom; 'perhaps' marks him as one example

explanation.surface: Dominic Cummings expected a peerage, but the monarch blocked it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominic Cummings was Boris Johnson's chief adviser, here standing for the name Dom.
explanation.definitionFit: A dukedom is the rank of duke, the highest grade of the British peerage.

clue.text: Greeting surprises Sikh hosts from behind

indicators.note: read from behind means read from the end back to the start
to host is to contain, so the answer sits within the words before

parts.note: the last letter of surprises and the first three of Sikh

explanation.surface: A Sikh is taken aback by a welcome from someone approaching from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a common way of greeting someone, with the lips on the cheek.

clue.text: Rating's announced for electrical unit

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, so we go by how the words are pronounced

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, a seaman

explanation.surface: A naval rank is called out over the electrical system.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy a rating is a sailor below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The siemens is the SI unit of electrical conductance, named after Werner von Siemens.

clue.text: Doctor's notes showing Spooner's treatment given to immoral chef

indicators.note: Rev Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening consonants trade places

parts.note: base means immoral and a cook is a chef

explanation.surface: A doctor's records reveal how an unethical chef was treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment' fits the doctor, but here it is Spooner's habit of swapping initial sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A casebook is a record kept by a doctor or lawyer of the cases handled.

clue.text: Legendary like the Beatles were first

parts.note: the Beatles were the Fab Four
to lead is to be first

explanation.surface: The Beatles were legendary because they got there first.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabled means celebrated in story and fable, famous enough to be legendary.

clue.text: Rose runs after very naughty boy, wanting his name

indicators.note: after means coming later, so this letter is placed at the end
wanting means lacking, so the abbreviation for name is removed from him

parts.note: Monty Python's Life of Brian: he's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy
N is the abbreviation for name
R is runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A rose bush is placed after a badly behaved boy who has lost his name tag.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous line from Monty Python's Life of Brian identifies the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a wild prickly shrub, especially the dog rose or sweetbriar.

clue.text: Transfer of jailed mob due in 2012, say

indicators.note: a transfer moves things to new places, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, ready to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gang in prison is due to be moved in 2012.
explanation.walkthrough: '2012, say' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II marked sixty years on the throne in 2012, an example of that anniversary celebration.

clue.text: Lose head in fight on the town

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper in a scrap during a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out means away from home socialising, as when out enjoying a night on the town.

clue.text: Decided where to sleep if homeless?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: firmly set on a purpose
second meaning, read as two words: inside a canvas shelter, a place to sleep with no house

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the second meaning; the question mark flags that wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent as an adjective means resolved or determined, a firm decision having been made.

clue.text: One taking hill in second/first?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the joined pair that follows

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a tor is a rocky hill
1st written out as I-S-T, with I as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A driver changing between second and first gear to climb a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash lets 'second/first' read both as gear choices and as two separate pieces either side of the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a car driver, who may drop to a low gear to climb a steep slope.
